successors.name: Spanish Empire
successors.text: the city, 'peacefully transferred to Spanish hands'

ledger.x: 300 BC: the first pyramid is raised at Cholula.
650: Cacaxtla and Xochitécatl rise inside what had been Cholula's hinterland.

c. 700: the Gulf Coast Olmeca-Xicallanca take over Cholula and make it their capital. In 'The Tlachihualtepetl phase (CE 700–1200)' 'Cholula was taken over by the Gulf Coast group known as the Olmeca-Xicallanca, who made it their capital'; 'residents abandoned the Great Pyramid in the 8th century' (Great Pyramid…

c. 650–750: Cholula falls and Cacaxtla becomes 'the hegemonic power in this part of the Tlaxcala–Puebla valley'. The Cacaxtla page: 'the fall of the nearby city Cholula (c. 650 – 750)'. The year is the end of the page's range; the zone is the researcher's. The city of Cholula (10 km) is excluded: it stays Cholula's as…

c. 900: Cacaxtla's 'ascendancy came to an end around 900 CE and, by 1000, the city had been abandoned'; the pages do not say who took the valley. Cholula, the Olmeca-Xicallanca capital through 1200, is the obvious heir; bridging event at confidence 1. Re-read: the Olmeca-Xicalanca page is silent on the end of Cacaxtla…

wars.name: Cholula massacre
wars.outcome: 'In 1519, the Tlaxcalans led Cortés and his troops to Cholula' to punish the city for joining the Aztecs; the city submitted.

certainty.note: A city-state hinterland drawn as a radius; no treaty lines.
